extracted.intended_audience: volunteer judges at the Youth Speaks Teen Poetry Slam (judging poets ages 13–19)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and evaluation standards for volunteer judges at the Youth Speaks Teen Poetry Slam, asking judges to score teen poems across preliminaries, semi-finals, and finals using three primary criteria and procedural rules to ensure fairness and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Quality of the Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: One of three primary criteria; judges assess the intrinsic quality of the poem's writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges may consider clever usages of language, uniqueness of point-of-view or topic, clarity of metaphor, rhyme scheme, or other aspects they personally value. The page explicitly allows different emphases (e.g., language vs. content) as long as the judge remains fair and consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Quality of the Performance
rubrics_metrics.description: One of three primary criteria; judges assess how the poem is performed on stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance criteria can include choreography, sound of the voice, passion in the delivery, and physical movement. Judges may prioritize any of these elements, provided they apply the same standard across all poems they score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of the Work
rubrics_metrics.description: One of three primary criteria; judges evaluate the poem's subject matter and the idea behind it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content includes the passion behind the idea and the poem's topic or theme. The document notes some judges may focus primarily on content as their definition of 'strong writing.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness and Consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Core expectation: judges should be fair and consistent in applying their personal standards throughout the event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges are told to determine their own standard of excellence but must maintain that standard across the night and across rounds. Consistency is emphasized repeatedly as the key to good judging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge Role and Tone — Encourager of Young Writers
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges should think of themselves as encouragers of young writers (ages 13–19) and help set a positive tone for the evening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance includes clapping, laughing, crying, standing up and jumping around as desired; accept that you may be booed; overall be supportive and set the tone for the show.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate Scoring Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Scores must be recorded immediately following each performance and submitted as directed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not hold scores up. Jot your score on the provided index card immediately after the poem ends and pass it to the host, who will call out scores from low to high. Scores are anonymous; no one will know what scores you gave any poem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time Limit for Poems
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance length restriction that affects judging context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poems will be no longer than 3 minutes 30 seconds (3:30). Judges should expect a variety of topics within that time limit when evaluating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust Expectations by Round and Experience Level
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that poets' experience and polish vary by round and adjust judgements accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminaries often feature many first-timers and raw, exciting writing with surprises; Finals feature highly practiced performers. Judges should be mindful of these differences when scoring across rounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Score Inflation ('Don't give everyone a ten')
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance to resist crowd pressure to give uniformly high scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The crowd often wants all 10's; judges are explicitly reminded that while high scores are welcome, they cannot give everyone a ten and should be selective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score Creep Awareness and Mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize the common phenomenon where scores rise as the show progresses and use provided tools/procedures to mitigate it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document defines 'score creep' (scores rising as the show advances), notes that it 'happens every time,' and states mitigation measures: poets who go earlier in the first round go late in the second, and judges are given an individual scoresheet to keep track of earlier scores (optional but recommended) to help keep scoring consistent.
